'''Olaf O. Storaasli''' is a scientist & engineer who worked at [[NASA Langley Research Center|NASA]][https://larcalumni.org/about-the-laa/]),  [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]][https://www.ornl.gov/group/ft]), [[Centrus Energy]], & [http://www.synective.se Synective Labs]. At NASA, he led a hardware, software & applications teams to successfully develop one of NASA's first parallel computers, the [[finite element machine]], & developed rapid matrix equation algorithms tailored for high-performance computers to harness [[FPGA]] & GPU accelerators to solve science & engineering applications. He was a graduate advisor & instructor at the [[University of Tennessee]], [[George Washington University]] & [[Christopher Newport University]].

==Education==

Storaasli received a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in physics, mathematics, & French at [[Concordia College (Moorhead)|Concordia College]] (1964). He went on to earn an [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] in [[mathematics]] at [[University of South Dakota]] (1966) and a [[Ph.D.]] in [[engineering mechanics]] at [[North Carolina State University|NCSU]] (1970). He was a postdoctoral fellow at the [[Norwegian University of Science & Technology]] ([https://web.archive.org/web/20180117131542/http://73.121.39.212:8080/~olaf/OS/www/nasa/Thompson.jpg] (1984–85]) & the [[University of Edinburgh]]([https://olaftn.com/NASA/Awards/2008epcc.pdf 2008]).

==Research==
He developed, tested and documented [[Parallel Computing|parallel]] analysis software to speed [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] equation solution to simulate physical & biological behavior on advanced-computer architectures (e.g. NASA's [https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20040086655/downloads/20040086655.pdf GPS] solver based on prior [[Finite element machine]] and rapid parallel analysis of [[Space Shuttle Solid Rocket Booster|Space Shuttle SRB]] redesign earned [[Cray]]'s 1st GigaFLOP Performance [https://web.archive.org/web/20090226230512/http://www.geocities.com/olafva/SRB.jpg Award] at Supercomputing '89).

* Engineering Applications on NASA's FPGA-based Hypercomputer, 7th MAPLD, Washington, D.C., Sept 2004.
* Large-Scale Analysis, Design and Intelligent Synthesis Environments, Elsevier Sciences, 2000.
* Large-Scale Analysis & Design on High-Performance Computers & Workstations, Elsevier Sciences, 1998.
* Large-Scale Structural Analysis for High-Performance Computers & Workstations, Pergamon Press 1994.
* Parallel Computational Methods for Large-Scale Structural Analysis & Design, Pergamon Press 1993.
* Parallel Methods on Large-Scale Structural Analysis & Physics Applications, Pergamon Press 1991.
